rationale: The available literature provided in the SOURCES block directly supports the cohort of 8 individuals with de novo putative loss-of-function (pLoF) variants in TAF4 presenting with neurodevelopmental disorder and intellectual disability from Janssen et al. (2022). However, Bertoli-Avella et al. (2021) is not present in the provided sources to verify the 2 additional probands or their clinical phenotype frequencies. Furthermore, Janssen et al. (2022) explicitly states that 'TAF4 has not been described to date as a monogenic disease gene,' conflicting with the assertion that a unified 10-proband baseline across both studies can be verified from the available literature.

evidence.text: Janssen et al. (2022) describes a cohort of eight individuals carrying de novo putative loss-of-function (pLoF) variants in TAF4 who present with phenotypes consistent with a neurodevelopmental disorder, including intellectual disability, abnormal behavior, and facial dysmorphisms.

source.title: De novo putative loss‐of‐function variants in TAF4 are associated with a neuro‐developmental disorder
source.quote: We here present a cohort of eight individuals, each carrying de novo putative loss-of-function (pLoF) variants in TAF4 and expressing phenotypes consistent with a neuro-developmental disorder (NDD). Common features include intellectual disability, abnormal behavior, and facial dysmorphisms.

evidence.text: Janssen et al. (2022) states that TAF4 had not been previously described as a monogenic disease gene prior to their 8-individual series, and no data from Bertoli-Avella et al. is provided in the available sources to independently confirm the 2 probands or calculate a combined 10/10 penetrance.

source.title: De novo putative loss‐of‐function variants in TAF4 are associated with a neuro‐developmental disorder
source.quote: TAF4 has not been described to date as a monogenic disease gene. We here present a cohort of eight individuals, each carrying de novo putative loss-of-function (pLoF) variants in TAF4 and expressing phenotypes consistent with a neuro-developmental disorder (NDD).

conflicts: Janssen et al. (2022) describes a cohort of exactly 8 individuals with de novo pLoF variants and notes TAF4 had not been previously described as a monogenic disease gene, whereas the hypothesis posits an established unified denominator of 10 including 2 probands from Bertoli-Avella et al. (2021), which is not present in the provided sources.

new_directions.question_text: What are the specific phenotypic breakdowns and variant positions of the two probands reported in Bertoli-Avella et al. (2021) compared to the 8 probands in Janssen et al. (2022)?
new_directions.rationale: Directly evaluating the primary text of Bertoli-Avella et al. (2021) is necessary to determine whether their clinical assessment meets standardized HPO criteria for intellectual disability and whether their variants are true de novo pLoF alleles.

new_directions.question_text: Are there non-penetrant or milder neurodevelopmental presentations associated with TAF4 loss-of-function variants in general population databases (e.g., gnomAD)?
new_directions.rationale: Ascertainment bias from neurodevelopmental sequencing cohorts can artificially inflate penetrance of intellectual disability to 100%.
